repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body: --- ##### Was generative AI tooling used to co-author this PR? - [x] Yes - claude sonnet ## Summary This PR extends `GlueJobOperator` for durable execution (AIP-103): on Airflow 3.3+, the job run id is persisted to task state store immediately after submission, so a worker crash and retry reconnects to the run already executing in Glue instead of starting a new one. ## How it works today `GlueJobOperator`'s `resume_glue_job_on_retry` mechanism has two tiers: an XCom cached run id (fast path), falling back to a paginated scan of the job's run history tagged by task UUID. I reproduced twice against real AWS Glue that the fast path never fires on Airflow 3.x: the server clears a task instance's XComs before every non-deferral attempt, so the cached id is always gone by the time the next retry looks for it. Every retry was paying for the full scan regardless, and the scan itself returned the first UUID match regardless of state, so an earlier terminated run could mask an active one underneath it. ## Why `resume_glue_job_on_retry` already tries to do this via XCom, falling back to a scan of the job's run history when XCom is empty. Confirmed against real AWS Glue (killed the worker mid-poll, twice, under two different kill methods) that the XCom fast path never fires on Airflow 3.x: the server clears a task instance's XComs before every non-deferral attempt (`task_instances.py`'s `xcom_keys_to_clear`), so by the time the next retry looks for the cached id it's already gone. Every retry pays for the full paginated scan regardless of timing, not just the narrow crash-before-push window the mechanism's original PR (#62560) was written to cover. The scan itself also has a latent bug: it returns the first task-UUID match regardless of state, so an earlier terminated run can mask a still-active one further down the page. Not fixed in this PR -- see Scope below. This matters more for Glue than for most `ResumableJobMixin` ports: a Glue job's `concurrent_run_limit` defaults to `1`, so a duplicate submission doesn't just waste compute, it fails outright with `ConcurrentRunsExceededException` and the task keeps retrying against a run it can never observe. ## What changed - `GlueJobOperator` now inherits `ResumableJobMixin`. On Airflow 3.3+, the mixin checks task state store before doing anything else: an active run reconnects directly (one `get_job_state` call), a succeeded or externally stopped run returns without resubmitting, a terminal run resubmits fresh. - The **existing** XCom-then-scan mechanism is kept exactly as it was, relocated into `submit_job` (the mixin only calls `submit_job` when task state has nothing usable). This is what Airflow <3.3 runs on entirely, and what 3.3+ falls back to as a one-time bootstrap for a run started before this upgrade, or before task state store had anything persisted. - `durable` is fully inert below Airflow 3.3: setting it explicitly (`True` or `False`) only emits a `UserWarning` that it has no effect there, since the task state store it relies on doesn't exist yet. This is deliberate -- it avoids a `durable` parameter that promises real crash recovery on a version where it structurally can't deliver it (the same concern raised against the sibling KPO port at #71492, where `durable` is currently wired straight into the old mechanism regardless of Airflow version). - `resume_glue_job_on_retry` is deprecated in favour of `durable` (`AirflowProviderDeprecationWarning`). The warning fires on **every** supported Airflow version -- removal is tied to this provider's own release schedule, not to which Airflow version the caller happens to run, so staying silent below 3.3 would mean some users never see the warning before the parameter disappears. On Airflow 3.3+ its value maps onto `durable`, which is a real, working replacement there. Below 3.3, `durable` itself does nothing (per the point above), so the warning message says so explicitly rather than telling that user to switch to something currently inert for them; `resume_glue_job_on_retry` remains the only way to get this behavior until the provider's minimum supported Airflow version reaches 3.3, at which point the parameter can be removed outright. - A run `STOPPED` outside Airflow (e.g. cancelled manually) is treated as a success rather than resubmitted -- the work is genuinely finished, just not the way the task expected -- with a warning logged. Matches how `GlueJobHook.job_completion` and `GlueJobCompleteTrigger` already treat `STOPPED`. - Deferrable takes precedence over durable, unchanged in spirit from today: the Triggerer already tracks the run across the wait, so the run id isn't persisted to task state on that path. ## Behaviour change `durable` is owned by the mixin and defaults to `True`, but that default only has an effect on Airflow 3.3+. There, a Dag that never touched `resume_glue_job_on_retry` goes from "always resubmit on retry" to "reattach on retry" with no code change. Below 3.3, nothing changes for such a Dag: `durable`'s default is meaningless there, and behavior matches the pre-existing `resume_glue_job_on_retry=False` default exactly. Documented in `providers/amazon/docs/changelog.rst` and `providers/amazon/docs/operators/glue.rst`. ## Scope Deliberately left alone, all pre-existing, none introduced by this PR: - The scan's first-match-regardless-of-state bug described above. - `GlueJobHook._handle_state` treats only `FAILED`/`TIMEOUT` as failure, so AWS's terminal `ERROR`/`EXPIRED` states fall through to "keep polling" and the sync poll loop never exits on them. - `ResumableJobMixin.execute_resumable`'s reconnect path returns `poll_until_complete`'s `None` instead of calling `get_job_result`, unlike the other two paths. Not touched here (no task-sdk change) -- every method instead sets `self._job_run_id`, and `execute()` returns that directly. ## Why `task_state_store` is a better crash recovery mechanism **1. It survives retries while XCom does not.** Airflow clears all XComs before each retry attempt. `task_state_store` is built specifically to persist across retries. **2. One call vs. a full scan.** Store hit -> single `get_job_state` call. Scan -> paginates the entire job run history, 50 at a time. **3. No ambiguity.** Store returns the exact id you saved. The scan matches by tag and can pick a stale run if an older one shares the tag. ## Testing Uploaded this script on AWS Glue and created an _ETL JOB_ there: ```python import sys import time def get_arg(name, default=None): flag = f"--{name}" if flag in sys.argv: i = sys.argv.index(flag) if i + 1 < len(sys.argv): return sys.argv[i + 1] return default task_uuid = get_arg("airflow_task_uuid", "") sleep_total = int(get_arg("sleep_seconds", "600")) print(f"argv: {sys.argv}", flush=True) print(f"airflow_task_uuid = {task_uuid}", flush=True) print(f"sleeping for {sleep_total}s", flush=True) elapsed = 0 while elapsed < sleep_total: time.sleep(15) elapsed += 15 print(f"alive {elapsed}/{sleep_total}s uuid={task_uuid}", flush=True) print("done", flush=True) ``` Using this DAG: ```python from datetime import datetime, timedelta from airflow.providers.amazon.aws.operators.glue import GlueJobOperator from airflow.sdk import DAG with DAG( dag_id="glue_job_trial", schedule=None, start_date=datetime(2024, 1, 1), catchup=False, ) as dag: run_glue = GlueJobOperator( task_id="run_glue", job_name="airflow_durable_test", aws_conn_id="aws_default", region_name="us-east-1", durable=True, script_args={"--sleep_seconds": "900"}, wait_for_completion=True, deferrable=False, verbose=True, retries=3, retry_delay=timedelta(seconds=20), ) ``` ### Case 1: Crash Recovery after worker crash Launched the DAG: Glue Job: State Store: Brought the worker down, see that the airflow task instance goes to retry state Reconnects to same job ### Case 2: Stop a run which was submitted from Glue Console, there should be no resubmit ### Case 3: `wait_for_completion=False` persists to state store Update task to: ```python run_glue = GlueJobOperator( task_id="run_glue", job_name="airflow_durable_test", aws_conn_id="aws_default", region_name="us-east-1", durable=True, script_args={"--sleep_seconds": "900"}, wait_for_completion=False, deferrable=False, verbose=True, retries=3, retry_delay=timedelta(seconds=20), ) ``` --- * Read the **[Pull Request Guidelines](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst#pull-request-guidelines)** for more information. Note: commit author/co-author name and email in commits become permanently public when merged. * For fundamental code changes, an Airflow Improvement Proposal ([AIP](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW/Airflow+Improvement+Proposals)) is needed. * When adding dependency, check compliance with the [ASF 3rd Party License Policy](https://www.apache.org/legal/resolved.html#category-x). * For significant user-facing changes create newsfragment: `{pr_number}.significant.rst`, in [airflow-core/newsfragments](https://github.com/apache/airflow/tree/main/airflow-core/newsfragments). issue.body:
Deferrable tasks need to decide whether to reuse a remote job without waiting in the worker. Today that decision also starts polling. This separates the decision and ID persistence from polling so callers can reuse them without blocking.

Synchronous operators retain the combined workflow. Reconnected tasks now return their job result instead of losing it as `None` in XCom.

Related: https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/71485. Runner consumer: https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/68955.

## Testing

The probe uses the real mixin with the existing test operator and in-memory job/state stand-ins, not a live service. It checks that deciding does not submit or poll, then checks the result of reconnecting.

From the PR checkout, save the Python below as probe.py:

<details><summary>Probe, commands and selected output</summary>

```python
from proof_fixture import ConcreteResumableOperator, FakeTaskState, make_context
operator = ConcreteResumableOperator(task_id="proof")
operator._status_map["job-001"] = "RUNNING"
context = make_context(FakeTaskState({"test_job_id": "job-001"}))
if hasattr(operator, "get_resume_decision"):
    decision = operator.get_resume_decision(context)
    print(f"decision={decision.action.value} submitted={operator.submitted_ids} polled={operator.polled_ids}")
else:
    print("non-blocking decision: unavailable")
result = operator.execute_resumable(context)
print(f"result={result!r} submitted={operator.submitted_ids} polled={operator.polled_ids}")
```

```bash
git show 4e62cb149b:task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/bases/test_resumablejobmixin.py > proof_fixture.py
F=task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/bases/resumablejobmixin.py
for ref in 4e62cb149b 856061a9; do
  git checkout "$ref" -- "$F"
  uv run --project task-sdk python probe.py
done
```

Before:

```text
non-blocking decision: unavailable
result=None submitted=[] polled=['job-001']
```

After:

```text
decision=reconnect submitted=[] polled=[]
result='result-of-job-001' submitted=[] polled=['job-001']
```

</details>

The mixin suite was rerun. Earlier provider checks passed. The consumer driver is unavailable; runner integration had eight failures with either core and remains unverified.

issue.body:
closes: #71485

Summary
ResumableJobMixin.execute_resumable() bundled its crash-recovery decision
(read stored external ID, call get_job_status, apply is_job_active /
is_job_succeeded) together with submission and polling in one method.
Deferrable operators typically call submit_job directly from execute()
rather than execute_resumable(), so they had no way to reuse this decision
step and had to fall back to their own operator-specific bootstrap scans
on every retry (e.g. GlueJobOperator's task-UUID scan).

Root cause
The reconnect-decision logic was private to execute_resumable(), with no
public entry point that returned "reconnect / already succeeded / submit
fresh" without also submitting, persisting, or polling.

Fix
Extracted the decision block into a new public method,
resolve_reconnect(context) -> ResumeDecision, with identical logging,
metrics, and OpenTelemetry span attributes. execute_resumable() now just
calls resolve_reconnect() and acts on the result. A deferrable operator
can call resolve_reconnect() itself before defer() and again on a
deferred retry, reconnecting via the same task_state_store lookup instead
of an operator-specific scan.

issue.title: Add durable reconnect option to EmrServerlessStartJobOperator

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
This adds a `durable` option to `EmrServerlessStartJobOperator` that persists the submitted job run id to task state (Airflow 3.3+) and, on a retry or a manual clear/rerun, reconnects to the still-running (or already-succeeded) job run instead of submitting a duplicate.

## Motivation

On a clear/retry today, a deferrable EMR Serverless task re-runs `execute()` and starts a brand-new job run, so the original hourly-billed Spark job is duplicated. `GlueJobOperator` already avoids this via its `durable` option; EMR Serverless had no equivalent, so the two Spark-submitting operators behaved differently on the same user action. This brings them into line.

## Behaviour

- `durable=True` → on a retry or clear, reconnect to the still-running job (no duplicate, no re-bill). If the prior run already **succeeded**, return it without re-running. If the prior run is terminal-failed, submit fresh.
- `durable=False` (default) → unchanged behaviour.

Has no effect on Airflow < 3.3 (task state unavailable), where it degrades to a fresh submit.

**Clearing on Airflow 3.4+.** Since #72100, clearing a task discards its task state unless `keep_task_state` is set ("retries resume, clearing starts over"). So `durable` reconnects on retries and on clears that keep task state; a plain clear submits a new run, and a task that had already succeeded runs again. With `cancel_on_kill` off (the `durable` default in deferrable mode) the old run keeps going after a plain clear, so set `cancel_on_kill=True` to stop it. The CLI `airflow tasks clear` and clearing a whole Dag run still keep task state (#72929). `GlueJobOperator`'s deferrable path differs here because it finds the previous run by a task-UUID scan rather than task state, so it reattaches on any clear.

### `durable` with `cancel_on_kill` in deferrable mode

In deferrable mode the trigger's `on_kill` cancels the job on any user action, and it cannot tell a clear (which re-runs the task) from mark failed/success. On clear the worker re-executes `execute()` **before** the triggerer calls `on_kill` (measured ~0.5s earlier on live AWS), so a durable retry would reconnect to a run `on_kill` then cancels, failing the task. The two options are resolved the same way as `GlueJobOperator`'s `durable` with `stop_job_run_on_kill` (#73702):

- `durable=True` with `cancel_on_kill` **unset** turns `cancel_on_kill` off (deferrable, Airflow 3.3+ only), so reconnect-on-clear is what `durable` gives by default. Marking the task failed then leaves the job running, as with Glue's default.
- `durable=True` with `cancel_on_kill=True` **set explicitly**: a retried try does not reconnect. It cancels the stored run if it is still active and submits a fresh one. Unlike Glue, it does not wait for the cancellation to finish, since EMR Serverless has no per-job concurrency limit.
- Below Airflow 3.3 `durable` does nothing, so `cancel_on_kill` keeps its default there.
- Synchronous mode is unchanged: `cancel_on_kill` does not apply (the operator's own `on_kill` always cancels).

A stored run that already succeeded is returned before the application is started, so clearing a finished task does not wake up a stopped application.

## Validated on live AWS

EMR Serverless (ap-northeast-2), standalone Airflow on `main` (3.4.0.dev, before #72100) plus this branch, Spark sleep job:

| config | behaviour after clear | result |
|---|---|---|
| `durable=True` (cancel_on_kill forced off) | reconnect to the running run | PASS — 1 run |
| `durable=True`, cleared after success | reconnect to the succeeded run, no re-run | PASS — 1 run |
| `durable=False` (baseline) | new run submitted, old not reconnected | reproduces the pre-existing gap — 2 runs |
| `durable=True` + `cancel_on_kill=True` (deferrable) | cancel the previous run, submit fresh | not yet re-validated after this change |

## Implementation notes / reviewer questions

1. **Default value.** Kept `durable=False`; `GlueJobOperator` defaults `durable=True` on 3.3+. Happy to raise the default if preferred.
2. **Why not `ResumableJobMixin`.** `execute_resumable` blocks on `poll_until_complete`, so it is synchronous-only and cannot serve the deferrable path — the case that matters for EMR Serverless. The reconnect is implemented directly in `execute()` (covering both the synchronous and deferrable paths), but it is a faithful port of the mixin: the same decision tree (active → reconnect / succeeded → skip / terminal → resubmit) and the same persist timing with `retention` omitted (30-day `[state_store] default_retention_days`, matching the mixin). Related: #71485.

## Testing

- New unit tests: reconnect-to-active, reconnect-to-succeeded (returns before the application start), resubmit-on-terminal, fresh-submit persistence, no-store fallback, `durable=False` no-op, deferrable reconnect, deferrable `durable` + explicit `cancel_on_kill=True` cancelling the previous run and submitting fresh (including when the cancel is rejected and when the run already succeeded), and the `cancel_on_kill` default with `durable` on and below Airflow 3.3.
- `test_emr_serverless.py` + EMR trigger suites pass locally, except two untouched `TestEmrServerlessStopOperator` tests that error on a local venv import (`airflow_shared` in the `caplog` fixture) and pass in another checkout.
- Live-AWS matrix above (the explicit `cancel_on_kill=True` row still to be re-run).
- `prek` pre-commit hooks and provider `mypy` (`breeze run mypy`) on the changed files pass.
